name: Hotel Wailea
summary: A 72-suite, adults-only Relais & Châteaux retreat on 15 hillside acres: intimate, residential and far removed from Hawai‘i’s family mega-resort pattern.
priceNote: No usable Oct 5–11 checkout quote was captured. This is an estimated all-in planning range; request a refundable six-night total including taxes and any mandatory charges. Andaz Maui is intentionally excluded from this set because its posted Sep 7–Nov 14, 2026 renovation overlaps the stay.
weather: Warm, trade-wind early October; south Maui is among the drier island microclimates, with hot beach days and occasional brief showers.
route: MIA → OGG requires a connection; OGG → SFO has nonstop service on selected schedules. Wailea is roughly 25–35 minutes from OGG.
honestCatch: It is not beachfront and has a smaller on-property activity campus; the value case depends on a live all-in quote below the hard ceiling.

name: Kona Village, A Rosewood Resort
summary: Standalone kauhale, lava-and-ocean landscape, cultural and marine programming, and an Asaya spa built into the lava flow create the strongest sense of place in the field.
priceNote: No exact-date rate or availability was returned. This high, wide all-in estimate reflects the premium room product and Hawaiʻi taxes; obtain a written six-night total before considering it within budget.
weather: Hot and generally dry on the leeward Kona coast in early October, though Kona storms can interrupt the normal pattern as the wetter season approaches.
route: MIA → KOA requires a protected mainland connection; KOA → SFO has nonstop options. The resort is roughly 20 minutes from KOA.
honestCatch: It can exceed the $2,500 all-in ceiling, and recent evidence is mixed on service and food-and-beverage execution despite the extraordinary setting.

name: 1 Hotel Hanalei Bay
summary: The field’s most dramatic setting pairs Hanalei Bay views with serious wellness, three heated pools, ocean access and nature-led design.
bestRoom: Ocean View Terrace King with a confirmed real terrace
priceNote: A third-party Oct 5–11 signal showed $9,382.63 before tax for six nights, with the $59 nightly resort fee included; the all-in range adds the listed tax stack and valet allowance. Reconfirm directly. Signature Welina Terrace is closed Oct 5–30, 2026, with a pop-up replacing it.
weather: Warm and lush, with the highest rain risk in this Hawaiʻi set as Princeville moves into the wetter season; showers can be localized but materially affect a beach-first stay.
route: MIA → LIH requires a connection; LIH → SFO has nonstop options. Princeville is roughly 50–60 minutes from LIH.
honestCatch: Welina Terrace is closed for the entire stay, service consistency has drawn credible complaints, and many standard rooms lack a true terrace; book only a confirmed terrace room on a refundable rate.

name: Four Seasons Resort Hualālai
summary: Extensively renovated rooms, five restaurants, King’s Pond, marine-biologist programming, manta snorkeling, golf and volcanic excursions make this the safest full-service choice.
priceNote: No Oct 5–11 quote was captured. Public non-date signals ran from roughly $1,330 for standard rooms to above $2,000 for ocean views before the full Hawaiʻi tax stack; this is an all-in planning range.
weather: Hot, sunny leeward-coast weather is the baseline, with low rain risk relative to Kauaʻi and windward locations.
route: MIA → KOA requires a connection; KOA → SFO has nonstops. The resort is roughly 15 minutes from KOA.
honestCatch: It is large and family-oriented, and the ocean-view category most worth booking may land at or above the hard all-in ceiling.

name: Mauna Lani, Auberge Collection
summary: A renovated Kohala Coast resort with a real spa, broad cultural and ocean programming, golf and a calm bay—capable without Hualālai or Kona Village pricing.
priceNote: No exact October quote was captured. A separate-date signal started near $848 including taxes and fees; this all-in planning range adds room-category spread plus the official $60 resort fee and likely $40 parking.
weather: Warm, dry and sunny on the leeward Kohala Coast, with among the best early-October weather odds in Hawaiʻi.
route: MIA → KOA requires a connection; KOA → SFO has nonstop options. Mauna Lani is about 30 minutes from KOA.
honestCatch: At 333 rooms it is a full resort, not a hideaway; the beach is a calm lagoon, and the $60 resort fee plus parking erodes the apparent value.

name: Four Seasons Resort Lānaʻi
summary: A quiet, high-service resort above Mānele Bay with a broad island program and genuine remove from the family-resort circuit.
priceNote: A Michelin-indexed non-date signal was about $1,567 with taxes. This broader all-in range is not proof of Oct 5–11 availability; obtain a cancellable quote. Eligible room bookings include round-trip Honolulu–Lānaʻi flights through 2027.
weather: Warm and generally dry around Mānele Bay, with trade winds and a lower rain risk than Kauaʻi’s north shore.
route: MIA → HNL requires a connection, followed by the included Lānaʻi Air sector when eligible; return positions through HNL before HNL → SFO.
honestCatch: The island isolation is romantic but creates the highest routing friction in the set, including a mandatory positioning flight before the mainland return.

quote.text: Round-trip flights from Honolulu are included in all room bookings through December 31, 2027 on Lanai Air.

name: The Lodge at Kukui‘ula
summary: A one-bedroom club bungalow delivers a private island home plus an adult pool, spa, farm, golf, racquets, dining and adventure programming.
bestRoom: One-Bedroom Platinum Club Bungalow with exact unit guaranteed
priceNote: Nearby-date entry inventory was around $1,182 with estimated taxes and fees. This all-in target includes a cushion for the official 15% destination fee, $150 reservation fee and damage waiver; exact Oct 5–11 inventory was not verified.
weather: Warm and comparatively dry in sunny Poʻipū; the south shore is the safer Kauaʻi weather bet in October.
route: MIA → LIH requires a connection; LIH → SFO has nonstops. The Lodge is roughly 25–35 minutes from LIH.
honestCatch: This is a residential/private-club product rather than a conventional hotel, it has no direct swimmable beach, and the 15% destination fee materially changes the total.

name: Sensei Lānaʻi, A Four Seasons Resort
summary: An adults-only upland retreat built around personalized wellness, private spa hales, movement, nutrition and unusually calm garden surroundings.
bestRoom: Koʻele Deluxe Room near the gardens
priceNote: No October price or availability was verified. This is a broad all-in estimate for planning only; wellness consultations, spa-hale time and premium programming may be additional.
weather: Cooler in the island uplands than Mānele Bay, with trade winds, cloud and brief showers possible.
route: MIA → HNL requires a connection and a Lānaʻi positioning flight; return requires the reverse before HNL → SFO.
honestCatch: It is inland rather than beachfront and more structured wellness retreat than romantic beach resort; choose it only if post-wedding recovery is the trip’s central purpose.

name: Mauna Kea Beach Hotel
summary: Fresh from a roughly $240 million transformation, Mauna Kea combines a superb swimmable crescent beach, new adult infinity pool and spa, manta viewing, golf, tennis and cultural programming.
priceNote: AFAR reported rates from $998 including breakfast for two, with other current signals around $1,100–$1,200 including taxes and fees. This is a non-date all-in target for a worthwhile ocean room.
weather: Warm, dry Kohala Coast conditions around 86°F/74°F historically, with low rainfall and excellent early-October odds.
route: MIA → KOA requires a connection; KOA → SFO has nonstops. The hotel is roughly 35–45 minutes from KOA.
honestCatch: It remains a multigenerational legacy resort rather than an intimate hideaway, and food-and-beverage consistency is the recurring weak spot.

name: Ko‘a Kea Resort on Poʻipū Beach
summary: A low-rise 121-room oceanfront hotel with couple-forward energy, Red Salt, yoga and beach access—Kauaʻi’s clearest conventional minimoon hotel.
priceNote: Michelin’s October calendar showed roughly $968 with free cancellation, but not a captured Oct 5–11 checkout. This all-in range allows for resort fee, parking and Hawaiʻi taxes; confirm the oceanfront premium.
weather: Warm and comparatively dry on Kauaʻi’s south shore, with better October reliability than Princeville.
route: MIA → LIH requires a connection; LIH → SFO has nonstops. Poʻipū is roughly 25–35 minutes from LIH.
honestCatch: The room hardware is slightly dated—dark wood, carpet and not-very-private lanais—and the pool and spa are compact. Book only oceanfront.

name: Halekulani
summary: A composed oceanfront classic with the strongest recent service signal, elegant rooms, La Mer and a calm pool culture despite its urban setting.
priceNote: No exact Oct 5–11 checkout was captured. This all-in planning range reflects generic public luxury-Waikīkī signals and room-category spread; reprice the Diamond Head category directly.
weather: Hot and generally sunny in leeward Honolulu, with brief showers possible and lower weather risk than Oʻahu’s North Shore.
route: MIA → HNL requires a connection; HNL → SFO has frequent nonstops. Waikīkī is roughly 25–45 minutes from HNL depending on traffic.
honestCatch: It is an urban Waikīkī grand dame with a small beach footprint, not a secluded resort; city and neighboring-hotel energy remain close.

name: Four Seasons Resort Oʻahu at Ko Olina
summary: A polished west-Oʻahu resort with a calm swimmable lagoon, serious spa and a valuable adults-only infinity pool that creates a genuine couple refuge.
bestRoom: Prime Oceanfront King, away from connecting-family inventory
priceNote: No exact-date quote was captured. This broad all-in planning range reflects generic luxury Ko Olina signals and meaningful category spread; confirm taxes, fees and room adjacency.
weather: Hot, sunny and dry on Oʻahu’s leeward coast, with very good early-October beach weather odds.
route: MIA → HNL requires a connection; HNL → SFO has frequent nonstops. Ko Olina is roughly 30–45 minutes from HNL.
honestCatch: The resort is highly family-oriented and sits beside Disney Aulani; explicitly request a quiet room without a connecting door and away from family-adjacent inventory.

name: The Ritz-Carlton Oʻahu, Turtle Bay
role: The North Shore activity base—bungalow only
summary: Turtle Bay’s landscape, surfing, horseback riding, golf, hiking and spa are compelling when paired with one of 42 waterfront Ocean Bungalows separated from the 408-room main building.
priceNote: The resort’s generic October average was around $940, but that does not price the only category recommended here. This all-in bungalow range is directional; eliminate it if the live bungalow total exceeds about $1,800.
weather: Warm and breezy on Oʻahu’s North Shore, with more passing showers and surf exposure than Ko Olina but less rain risk than Princeville.
route: MIA → HNL requires a connection; HNL → SFO has frequent nonstops. Turtle Bay is roughly 60–90 minutes from HNL depending on traffic.
honestCatch: It is compelling only in an Ocean Bungalow. The main wing is a large family-heavy legacy resort, and recent reviews repeatedly flag slow or uneven service and food.
